1. Education in Emergencies (EiE) & Learning Continuity
OGMC supports governments, UN agencies, and NGOs to design, implement, and strengthen Education in Emergencies (EiE) interventions that ensure safe, inclusive, and continuous learning for children and youth affected by conflict, displacement, disasters, and public health emergencies. Our work aligns with INEE Minimum Standards and focuses on access, protection, psychosocial support, teacher capacity development, and education system recovery in fragile contexts.
2. Climate Education & Resilience Programming
OGMC delivers climate-responsive education and resilience programs that integrate climate change adaptation, disaster risk reduction (DRR), and environmental sustainability into education systems and community learning. We support partners to mainstream climate education, strengthen school and community resilience, and promote locally grounded adaptation strategies aligned with SDG 13 and education sector priorities.
3. Monitoring, Evaluation, Accountability & Learning (MEAL)
OGMC provides comprehensive MEAL services to improve program quality, accountability, and learning. This includes results frameworks, indicator development, baseline and endline assessments, third-party monitoring, learning agendas, and evaluation studies. Our MEAL approaches are equity-focused, participatory, and evidence-driven, supporting adaptive management and informed decision-making.
4. Education Systems Strengthening & Policy Support
OGMC supports education sector planning, policy development, and system strengthening at national and sub-national levels. We work with ministries of education and development partners to align programs with Education Sector Plans (ESPs), strengthen data use, improve coordination, and enhance system resilience to shocks, in line with GPE and UNESCO frameworks.
5. Capacity Development & Technical Assistance
OGMC delivers targeted capacity strengthening and technical assistance for education stakeholders, including government officials, school leaders, teachers, and community actors. Our support focuses on EiE preparedness, climate adaptation, MEAL systems, safeguarding, and inclusive education, using practical, context-specific, and participatory learning approaches.
6. Knowledge Management, Research & Learning
OGMC supports partners to generate, document, and use knowledge through research, learning products, and evidence synthesis. Reach to Teach partners with State Governments through a formal Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) as a knowledge and technical partner to support the Education Department in designing and rolling out large-scale academic reforms.Our idea of scaling is rooted in system strengthening, deep consultation, and working from within the existing Government education system to reach all Government schools in the State. We scale by embedding ourselves within the State Education Department which enables us to work across every level. Rather than setting up parallel structures, we co-create all interventions, curriculum design, training frameworks, implementation tools, and monitoring mechanisms, with system actors. By doing so, we create scalable solutions by using the Department and its functionaries as the force multipliers and do not need to staff-up. This approach ensures that with a small and agile team, we achieve State-wide coverage from inception by leverage existing Government outreach, infrastructure, and personnel, while building the system‚Äôs own capacity to deliver, adapt and sustain. This leads to rollout at scale, sustainability and a lasting improvement at a systems level. As the ownership of the process lies with the Government, and we ensure institutionalisation, our design has a clear exit strategy supported by documentation and a systematic handover process.","SingleLine2":"Reach To Teach Foundation","MultiLine7":"","SingleLine3":"Manoranjan Nayak","MultiLine1":"Every child will have access to quality education to enable them to become confident social citizens with improved life chances","SingleLine5":"Chief Operating Officer","MultiLine2":"We strive to improve education outcomes by making learning joyful, working with governments, partners, parents and communities, with foundational learning skills at the core.","MultiLine3":"The Reach to Teach Foundation works with State Governments on strengthening Leaning Outcomes in Government schools at scale by focusing on the twin elements of experiential learning and designing for teacher led interventions. We currently work in four States‚Äì Gujarat, Haryana, Arunachal Pradesh and Meghalaya ‚Äì focusing on system realignment, scale and sustainability. Our work is based on design-led principles and we work with the Education Department and their functionaries and teachers to consult and design interventions collaboratively. This co-creation has led to ownership by the Department and we train district level functionaries and teachers through a ‚Äòdoing and learning‚Äô approach on the use of the material and tools thus collaboratively designed. These people in turn become the State‚Äôs feet on street, implementing our design across every school in the State. It is a fully hands on model and has several advantages, The implementation is by the Government system across all Government schools in a State leading to system change at scale. This allows for a small team at our end to drive large-scale improvement. {"Address_address2":"Pocket 9, Sector B, Vasant Kunj, New Delhi, Delhi 110070","Email":"ankit@idreamcareer.com","Address_address1":"2nd Floor, Boulder Box Building,","Website1":"https://www.linkedin.com/company/idreamcareer-com/","Website2":"","Number3":"498","Formula":"50","Number2":"20000000","Number1":"200000","MultiLine5":"iDreamCareer engages closely with government bodies through both financial and non-financial partnerships to support the institutionalization of career guidance within public education systems. Under financial agreements, iDreamCareer has directly implemented paid career guidance programs funded by government institutions, including RMSA Andhra Pradesh in 2018, CBSE in 2025, and the District Education Office, Sundargarh in Odisha in 2024, covering program design, deployment, and outcome monitoring. 

Alongside this, iDreamCareer has worked through several non-financial and grant-supported government partnerships focused on system design, capacity building, and piloting scalable models. This includes collaboration with EVGC Delhi, initially supported by Central Square Foundation, followed by UNDP and Tata Power DDL, to embed career guidance within Delhi government schools. iDreamCareer has also partnered with the Department of Secondary Education, Uttar Pradesh under a non-financial agreement with program funding provided by Mahindra Social Responsibility Foundation. In addition, iDreamCareer has engaged with New Delhi Municipal Council and Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation to support career guidance initiatives within municipal school systems; NDMC and BMC are among the richest municipal corporations in India, and these partnerships demonstrate iDreamCareer‚Äôs ability to work with financially strong urban local bodies as well as state education systems, combining public funding, external philanthropy, and technical expertise to enable scalable and sustainable adoption of career guidance.","SingleLine2":"iDreamCareer","MultiLine7":"iDreamCareer is a mission-driven social enterprise operating through a dual-entity structure that allows us to combine scale, sustainability, and impact. Our work is delivered through a for-profit entity, Medhavi Professional Services Pvt Ltd (branded as iDreamCareer), and a Section 8 not-for-profit organization, Aasman Foundation, which holds valid FCRA registration. This structure enables us to work seamlessly with governments, schools, CSR programs, and philanthropic funders, while ensuring financial sustainability and long-term system adoption.

Our social impact work is anchored under PathShila, which focuses on enabling equitable access to career guidance for students from government and underserved school systems, while advocating for the institutionalization of career counseling within public education. Across all our work, we leverage technology as a core enabler‚Äîusing digital platforms and AI to support students in receiving personalized guidance, empower counselors to deliver structured and efficient interventions, and help systems measure outcomes such as enrolment, persistence, and transitions. By combining on-ground delivery, capacity building, and technology, iDreamCareer works to move career guidance from fragmented interventions to a measurable, system-level solution that supports successful education-to-employment transitions at scale.","SingleLine3":"Manish Chourasia","MultiLine1":"To enable every learner‚Äîregardless of background‚Äîto make informed, confident, and aspirational education-to-employment decisions, and to unlock equitable economic mobility at scale.","SingleLine5":"Director PathShila","MultiLine2":"By 2030, iDreamCareer aims to enable informed, equitable, and aspirational education-to-employment transitions for over 11 million learners‚Äîreaching 1 million students through direct classroom and counseling programs and 10 million learners through system-level adoption with governments and institutions.","MultiLine3":"iDreamCareer‚Äôs core program is a system-led, technology-enabled career guidance model designed to support learners across school and post-school transitions while strengthening the institutions that serve them. The program combines direct student engagement, counselor capacity development, and digital platforms to ensure high-quality guidance at scale, and is delivered through paid partnerships with governments, schools, and institutions, making it sustainable and scalable.

At the center of the program is PathShila, iDreamCareer‚Äôs impact practice, which works primarily with students from government and low-income schools. PathShila delivers structured career guidance directly to students while advocating for the adoption of career counseling within government education systems. Through partnerships with state and district governments, NGOs, CSR programs, and philanthropic organizations, PathShila focuses on creating tangible, measurable impact and enabling career guidance to transition from short-term projects to a system-embedded public service.

Complementing this is BlueSpring, the private school practice, which works with private and international schools to integrate career guidance into the school ecosystem. BlueSpring delivers grade-wise, structured career guidance programs that support students and parents in making informed academic and career decisions, while helping schools institutionalize career guidance as a core offering.

To ensure long-term quality and scale, iDreamCareer runs Council, a capacity development initiative focused on strengthening the career counseling ecosystem. Council works with counselors across government systems, private schools, NGOs, and independent practice, providing training, certification, standardized frameworks, and continuous professional development to professionalize and scale high-quality career counseling.

All programs are enabled by iDC One, iDreamCareer‚Äôs AI-enabled career guidance platform, which supports students in receiving personalized guidance, enables counselors to deliver structured and efficient interventions, and allows schools and governments to monitor delivery quality, scale, and student transition outcomes over time. Together, these elements form a unified core program that moves career guidance from isolated interventions to a sustainable, system-level solution focused on informed education-to-employment transitions.","Address_zipCode":"110070","MultiLine4":"iDreamCareer‚Äôs impact is demonstrated through measurable improvements in Eligible Enrolment Ratio (EER) and stronger education-to-employment transitions driven by structured career guidance and system adoption. An independent impact evaluation conducted in December 2025 across five districts of Uttar Pradesh‚ÄîGhaziabad, Kanpur, Lucknow, Meerut, and Varanasi‚Äîfound that students in schools supported by iDreamCareer consistently recorded higher enrolment levels than comparison schools at both baseline and endline, with these differences being statistically significant (Pearson chi-square value of 29.96). Under financial agreements, iDreamCareer has directly implemented paid career guidance programs funded by government institutions, including RMSA Andhra Pradesh in 2018, CBSE in 2025, and the District Education Office, Sundargarh in Odisha in 2024, covering program design, deployment, and outcome monitoring.

This includes collaboration with EVGC Delhi, initially supported by Central Square Foundation, followed by UNDP and Tata Power DDL, to embed career guidance within Delhi government schools. iDreamCareer has also partnered with the Department of Secondary Education, Uttar Pradesh under a non-financial agreement with program funding provided by Mahindra Social Responsibility Foundation. Our work is delivered through a for-profit entity, Medhavi Professional Services Pvt Ltd (branded as iDreamCareer), and a Section 8 not-for-profit organization, Aasman Foundation, which holds valid FCRA registration. Our social impact work is anchored under PathShila, which focuses on enabling equitable access to career guidance for students from government and underserved school systems, while advocating for the institutionalization of career counseling within public education. Across all our work, we leverage technology as a core enabler‚Äîusing digital platforms and AI to support students in receiving personalized guidance, empower counselors to deliver structured and efficient interventions, and help systems measure outcomes such as enrolment, persistence, and transitions. At the center of the program is PathShila, iDreamCareer‚Äôs impact practice, which works primarily with students from government and low-income schools. PathShila delivers structured career guidance directly to students while advocating for the adoption of career counseling within government education systems. These findings confirmed the scale of the challenge and informed programme design, priorities, and capacity-building strategies.","SingleLine32":"The organization has onboarded a Monitoring and Evaluation Officer, but they are yet to begin collecting data given t hat work will begin this year.","Dropdown9":"Yes","MultiLine5":"we are legally registered with a working permit as a community-based organization in Mayuge Town council with registration number MYG24/DNGOMC/044","Dropdown10":"Yes","SingleLine3":"Saufa Chemutai","Email6":"saufachemutai@gmail.com","MultiLine7":"We are young and evolving organization, youth led and supporting young people to stay in school, complete their education and thrive to break the poverty levels, teenage pregnancy rampant in the community through psychosocial support.","Dropdown15":"GSF LinkedIn","SubForm":[{"firstName":"Ann","lastName":"Dechenne","jobTitle":"Chairperson Board","organisation":"Little by Little","email":"dechennea@gmail.com"},{"firstName":"Yusuf","lastName":"Kasakya","jobTitle":"Cofounder","organisation":"Leo EduPath","email":"ykasakya9@gmail.com"}],"Radio1":"Yes","Radio2":"Yes","SubForm1":[{"firstName":"Kayondo","lastName":"vicent","email7":"kayondovicent5@gmail.com"},{"firstName":"Asad","lastName":"Muyanja","email7":"muyanjaasad748@gmail.com"}],"SingleLine11":"The organisation was founded in response to observed challenges within rural and low-income school communities, where poverty, family instability, teenage pregnancy, neglect, and emotional distress significantly affect learner attendance, engagement, and academic performance. These psychosocial issues were identified as systemic and largely unaddressed within existing school structures, contributing to poor learning outcomes and high dropout rates.","SingleLine13":"The organisation is a youth-led, community-based initiative formally registered in December 2024, though its work began earlier at grassroots level. Most operational leadership is comprised of youth, supported by a small board providing strategic oversight. The organisation‚Äôs governance structure can be defined as a board-led, youth-driven model appropriate for an early-stage community-based organisation. It is overseen by a board that provides strategic direction, accountability, and oversight, while day-to-day operations are led by a predominantly youth-based executive and volunteer team. The board supports governance functions such as sustainability planning, policy oversight (including safeguarding), and long-term vision, while operational leadership focuses on programme design and implementation.","SingleLine15":"Eastern Uganda","SingleLine14":"Most operational leadership is comprised of youth, supported by a small board providing strategic oversight","Number4":"5","SingleLine17":"The organization's approach prioritises embedding psychosocial support systems within existing school and community structures to promote ownership and long-term sustainability. The current phase focuses on piloting and refining the model, with plans to scale gradually once effectiveness is demonstrated and systems are strengthened.","SingleLine28":"The organisation engaged district education leadership to share observations and evidence linking psychosocial wellbeing to academic performance. District authorities acknowledged the relevance of the approach, particularly in light of severe learner attrition between primary and secondary levels. This engagement led to support for piloting the model within schools as a potential response to persistent dropout and underperformance challenges.","SingleLine29":"Not yet available since the organization is still at the pilot phase.","MultiLine6":"The organization works with public primary and secondary schools. Initial interventions focused on creating emotionally safe and supportive classroom environments. These efforts resulted in improved learner attendance, engagement, and progression, including cases where learners previously stuck in repeated grades were able to advance. When expanded at school level, the approach showed broader improvements in attendance and performance, providing early evidence that psychosocial support can positively influence educational outcomes.","SingleLine8":"In 2025, the organization signed MoUs with the schoolsit will be working with in preparation for the work to start in 2026.","SingleLine34":"As a newly registered organisation, it remains at an early stage of institutional maturity, with most activities still in the pilot and system-design phase and limited evidence of long-term impact at scale. Current reliance on a small volunteer team may constrain operational capacity, monitoring, and growth. Scaling the model sustainably will require strengthened organisational systems, stable funding, and deeper partnerships with schools and authorities. The organisation‚Äôs success is also dependent on sustained buy-in from external stakeholders, and as it grows, there will be an increasing need to formalise governance, financial management, and monitoring and evaluation frameworks to support expansion and risk management.","SingleLine33":"The organisation demonstrates a strong and clearly articulated understanding of the psychosocial challenges affecting learners in underserved communities and positions emotional wellbeing as a critical driver of attendance, retention, and academic performance. Its approach is grounded in direct classroom experience and supported by baseline data, lending credibility to both problem identification and programme design. The programmatic model is coherent and holistic, combining safe spaces for learners, capacity building for teachers, and peer support mechanisms. In addition, the organisation shows strong safeguarding readiness, with comprehensive policies and high responsiveness during due diligence, and benefits from being youth-led with leadership that is closely aligned to the mission and context.","SingleLine35":"Joining GSF would support the organisation‚Äôs growth by providing access to a global peer network, shared learning, and practical insights from more established education organisations, helping to strengthen programme quality, safeguarding, governance, and monitoring systems. Membership would also enhance the organisation‚Äôs credibility and visibility, enabling stronger partnerships with funders, schools, and policymakers, while reducing early-stage risks and supporting responsible, sustainable scaling of its psychosocial support model within the education ecosystem.","SingleLine36":"The organisation would contribute to GSF by bringing strong grassroots insights and practitioner-led experience on integrating psychosocial and emotional wellbeing into school systems in low-resource contexts. Its data-informed, youth-led approach would add valuable perspectives to peer learning on learner wellbeing, safe spaces, and teacher capacity building, particularly in regions affected by poverty, instability, and high dropout rates. Through active participation in GSF‚Äôs community, the organisation would share lessons from piloting and embedding psychosocial support within existing school structures, contributing to collective learning, innovation, and the strengthening of holistic education approaches across the network.","SingleLine12":"the organisation is currently early-stage and primarily volunteer-led, with no formal long-term funding streams articulated at this stage. Its activities to date appear to have been supported through in-kind contributions, volunteer time, and modest, locally driven resources while systems, governance, and pilot programmes are being developed. The organisation is still in the foundational phase, focusing on designing sustainable models within existing school and community structures, and is expected to seek partnerships and external funding as it moves from piloting toward scale."}

","SingleLine11":"Perkins was founded in 1829 as the first school for the blind in the United States and the second globally. Over time, it evolved from a residential school model into a global organization focused on inclusive education. While it retains deep expertise in visual impairment, its current mandate supports children with a wide range of disabilities and promotes inclusive education systems that benefit all learners. Perkins operates a campus-based school in Boston for a small number of medically fragile learners while prioritizing inclusion in public education systems locally and internationally ","SingleLine13":"Perkins International Programs operates as one department within the larger Perkins organization, headquartered in Boston. Governance oversight is provided by an international committee that functions as a board for the international programs, with representation largely based in the U.S., complemented by international, gender, ethnic, and disability representation. In countries of operation, Perkins establishes local strategic working groups that serve an advisory function and ensure contextual alignment with national and community priorities ","SingleLine15":"Boston","SingleLine14":"Perkins is formally registered in the United States and India. In other countries of operation, programming is delivered through locally based consultants rather than registered country offices. ","Number4":"114","SingleLine17":"Perkins'  growth strategy prioritizes systemic impact over rapid expansion, focusing on developing model programs and centers of excellence that can be replicated by governments rather than expanding to every school or country. Expansion, including a return to Africa, is funding-dependent, not capacity-limited. Sustainability is achieved through long-term school engagement (3‚Äì5 years), strong government and university partnerships, and embedding inclusive practices within national systems, supported by a diversified base of institutional funders.","SingleLine28":"Rather than exporting a single curriculum model, Perkins works across multiple levels to strengthen inclusivity within existing national systems. This includes advising governments on curriculum adaptation, collaborating with universities on pre-service teacher education, and supporting schools to make national curricula accessible to learners with disabilities. The approach combines top-down policy engagement with bottom-up school-level implementation to ensure contextual relevance and sustainability .","SingleLine29":"USD 16,000 per school per year","MultiLine6":"Perkins primarily works with public schools, selected in partnership with governments and local authorities, serving children with disabilities alongside their peers in inclusive settings. While inclusion is the goal, a small number of special or medically complex learners are supported through specialized settings where mainstream schools are not yet equipped, with most program schools located in low- and middle-income countries.","SingleLine8":"Schools typically remain engaged in their programmes for three to five years, depending on their starting level and readiness, with some more advanced schools completing the process sooner once inclusive practices are sustainably embedded.","SingleLine33":"Perkins‚Äô main strengths include nearly 200 years of expertise in disability and inclusive education, a proven, data-driven school improvement model built around 150 quality indicators, strong government and university partnerships, and deep experience working in low- and middle-income countries with a focus on systemic change rather than short-term projects.","SingleLine34":"Ongoing funding constraints that limit geographic expansion (including re-entry into Africa), persistent stigma and negative attitudes toward disability, and the time and commitment required from schools and teachers to sustain multi-year quality improvement processes.","SingleLine35":"Perkins would benefit from peer learning and collaboration with other education-focused organizations, particularly around scaling systems change, sustainability, and inclusive education in diverse contexts. GSF would also provide a platform for strategic partnerships, shared learning on funding models and impact measurement, and opportunities to re-engage regions such as Africa through aligned members and funders.","SingleLine36":"Perkins would contribute deep technical expertise in inclusive and disability-responsive education, a rigorous quality improvement and monitoring framework, and nearly two centuries of institutional knowledge. It would add value through sharing evidence-based practices, tools, and lessons from long-term government partnerships, as well as mentoring peer organizations seeking to strengthen inclusive education at system level"}

{"Address_address2":"","Email":"sangeeta@apnishala.org","Address_address1":"Kamgar Nagar","Website1":"https://www.linkedin.com/in/sangeeta-zombade-31190818/","Website2":"","Number3":"700","Number2":"15000","Number1":"5000","MultiLine5":"Apni Shala partners with municipal and state governments towards Social-Emotional-Learning focussed schools. Currently, the organisation has partnered with Municipal Corporation of Greater Mumbai via (a) whole school partnership to build a model wellbeing-focused school and (b) to phase-wise transform schools via SEL in 15 schools, working with students, educators and caregivers. With Mira-Bhayandar Municipal Corporation, Apni Shala, along with other recognised Non-profit organisations is part of the Center of Excellence, where we are piloting SEL in one school, while also training educators and other stakeholders for mental wellbeing. Identification and Referral of Vulnerable Children:
Government officers, including Children‚Äôs Officers, Chiefs, Assistant Chiefs, and Nyumba Kumi (Ten-House) community leaders, support Safisha by identifying children who are out of school, at risk of dropping out, or living in extreme vulnerability. These children are formally referred to Safisha Africa School for admission and support
Vetting and Accountability:
Admissions are conducted through a community-based vetting process involving Nyumba Kumi leaders and local administration to confirm a family‚Äôs vulnerability. This ensures that Safisha‚Äôs services reach children who genuinely need support and strengthens transparency and accountability in program delivery
Registration and Oversight by the Ministry of Education:
Safisha Africa School is fully registered under the Ministry of Education and operates in compliance with national education policies and standards. The school follows the approved curriculum and is regularly monitored through education officers.
National Examinations and Transition to Public Secondary Schools:
Learners at Safisha sit for national examinations as required. Those who perform well are selected and enrolled into government secondary schools, ensuring continuity of education and full integration into the national education system.
Shared Commitment to Child Welfare and Retention:
Through this collaboration, Safisha and government partners jointly address school dropout, child protection, and access to education, ensuring children not only enroll in school but remain, perform well, and progress through the education system.

   Climate-resilient kitchen farming

    Environmental education to foster community responsibility","Address_zipCode":"00200","MultiLine4":"Impact of Safisha Africa Welfare Foundation
Since its founding in 2007, Safisha Africa Welfare Foundation has delivered life-changing, sustainable, and long-term impact** for children and women from under-resourced communities in Kenya.

Finally, we work in a range of countries including low and middle income countries.","SingleLine3":"Pragya Dhariwal","MultiLine1":"Every child and young person reaching their full potential","SingleLine5":"Chief Programs Officer","MultiLine2":"Our purpose is to start with the problem and work from the ground up ‚Äì partnering with stakeholders and systems to build joyful, measurable learning solutions to grow potential for children and youth.","MultiLine3":"At the core of our work is the support and adaptation of the Teaching at the Right Level (TaRL) approach, pioneered by Pratham in India. This is an evidence-based intervention designed to help children in Grade 3 and above catch up on foundational skills in reading and mathematics. The model works by grouping children based on their actual learning levels rather than their age or grade, enabling rapid progress over a short period.
This flexible approach can be adapted by NGOs, governments, and communities in various ways to suit local contexts.
To reduce the number of children reaching higher grades with foundational learning gaps, we have recently begun supporting adaptations of Pratham‚Äôs Leap Forward intervention. This targets children entering Grade 1 and those in Grades 1 and 2 through a combination of school- and community-based instructional and awareness building methods. The aim is to build critical foundational literacy and numeracy (FLN) skills early on, so that fewer children advance through the education system without these essential competencies.","Address_zipCode":"DE 19901","MultiLine4":"We define the impact of our work as improvements in foundational reading and math skills among children, achieved through government- and local partner‚Äëled TaRL programs.  Using simple, one‚Äëon‚Äëone tools inspired by ASER, children‚Äôs reading and maths skills are evaluated at baseline (at the start), midline (in the middle), and endline (at the end) of the intervention. Progress is often tracked by the percentage of children who can read at least a simple paragraph (Grade‚ÄØ1 level) and solve a basic subtraction problem by the end of the intervention.

The organisation emerged from the Community Childcare Project, which was funded by World Connect. This initial project focused on supporting home-based, centre-based, and community-based childcare providers through capacity building, advocacy, and the creation of peer support networks. The decision to formally register the organisation was driven by the need to attract further funding, institutionalise the work, and expand its impact. The core motivation behind the initiative is to address the significant policy and service gap affecting childcare for children aged 0‚Äì3 years in Nigeria, a group that is largely unsupported by existing education and social systems.","SingleLine12":"The organisation has so far received a single seed grant of approximately USD 4,000‚Äì4,400 from World Connect, which supported activities between 2024 and 2025. Although eligible for additional funding cycles under the same programme, the organisation did not apply immediately due to the need to first complete registration and demonstrate proof of concept. An additional USD 1,000 was contributed through the founder‚Äôs participation in the World Forum Global Leaders for Early Childhood Fellowship. At present, funding remains limited and largely grant-dependent.","SingleLine17":"The organisation‚Äôs programme model centres on training childcare providers who serve children aged 0‚Äì3 years, with some flexibility to include children up to age five depending on context. To date, three cohorts of childcare providers have successfully completed the programme, and preparations are underway for a fourth cohort. The training runs for ten weeks and is delivered through a blended model combining online learning and in-person sessions. The curriculum covers early childhood development, the five pillars of the Nurturing Care Framework, and practical guidance on childcare business formalisation and registration. Beyond direct training, the programme incorporates community-level impact through step-down training, where caregivers train peers, and parent awareness sessions focused on nutrition and responsive caregiving, sometimes reaching up to 100 parents per session. The long-term vision is to build credible evidence that can be used to advocate for policy reform and improved regulation of early childcare services. To improve sustainability, the organisation has introduced modest income-generating strategies, including charging a token registration and training fee, selling training materials such as caregiver‚Äìparent communication booklets, and supporting caregivers to generate income through the resale of nutrition products to parents. Despite these efforts, funding constraints remain a key limitation to scale and staffing.","SingleLine13":"The governance structure is currently lean and founder-led. The organisation is overseen by a three-member executive board comprising the founder and two senior women who serve in both governance and operational roles.Governance systems and policies are still evolving as the organisation transitions from an early-stage setup toward a more formal structure. ","SingleLine14":"The governance structure is currently lean and founder-led. The organisation is overseen by a three-member executive board comprising the founder and two senior women who serve in both governance and operational roles.","SingleLine28":"With regard to curriculum and regulation, the organisation does not rely on a nationally enforced early childhood curriculum for children aged 0‚Äì3, as existing government guidance is outdated and not actively implemented. Instead, the organisation has developed and continuously refined its own curriculum based on the globally recognised Nurturing Care Framework. While the childcare sector remains largely unregulated, NECCSI is registered with and accountable to the Ministry of Youth and Social Welfare, which oversees organisations working with vulnerable populations. However, the regulatory environment remains challenging, particularly for home-based childcare providers who are often penalised rather than supported.","SingleLine29":"From a costing perspective, the organisation estimates that it costs approximately USD 300 to fully train one childcare provider when training materials, facilitation, resources, and community engagement are factored in. This figure is based on internal calculations and remains indicative, as the organisation continues to refine its costing and financial models. The relatively high per-provider cost underscores the importance of securing sustainable funding streams.","MultiLine6":"Not Applicable","SingleLine8":"Not Applicable","SingleLine33":"Key strengths of the organisation include its deep integration within the communities it serves and its ability to deliver training in local languages and dialects. The programme is highly practical and experiential, making it accessible and relevant to caregivers with varying levels of formal education. Caregivers report strong engagement and increased confidence, and parents have responded positively to improved childcare practices. The founder‚Äôs background in childcare services, training, and child development further strengthens the organisation‚Äôs credibility and delivery model.","SingleLine34":"The organisation faces several challenges. Limited funding restricts the ability to hire staff, expand monitoring activities, and scale operations. The small team makes it difficult to conduct frequent field visits and provide ongoing hands-on support to caregivers. Additionally, while data is being collected, there is a recognised need for stronger research design, data analysis capacity, and structured learning systems to ensure the evidence generated can influence policy and attract larger funders.","SingleLine35":"The organisation sees membership in the Global Schools Forum as a critical opportunity to address these gaps. Its motivation for joining includes access to structured learning, technical support, peer exchange, and guidance on governance, monitoring and evaluation, costing, and sustainability. The organisation is also interested in potential incubator programmes and funding pathways that could enable responsible growth.","SingleLine36":"The organisation believes it can contribute meaningfully to the GSF community by sharing practitioner-level insights and data from Nigeria‚Äôs early childcare landscape, a context that is underrepresented in global evidence. The founder also brings strong teaching and mentoring skills and is keen to support peer learning within the community while contributing grounded, grassroots perspectives on early childhood care.","Number4":"11"}

The Sierra Leone Educators Association (SLEA) delivers a suite of integrated programs designed to holistically address the educational ecosystem. Our initiatives target students, teachers, schools, and communities to foster sustainable development and empower the next generation of leaders.

1. Literacy for All Program
We combat illiteracy through comprehensive, evidence-based initiatives that equip learners of all ages with foundational competencies in reading, writing, and critical comprehension. Our programs are implemented in both school and community settings to ensure nationwide impact.

2. Teacher Empowerment Initiative
Recognizing that teachers are the cornerstone of quality education, we provide continuous professional development. Our training modules focus on modern pedagogical techniques, subject-matter mastery, and psychosocial support, fostering a valued, motivated, and highly effective teaching force.

3. Human Rights & Civic Education
We are dedicated to weaving the principles of human rights and civic responsibility into the fabric of society. Through targeted engagement with students, youth, teachers, and parents, we build a culture of awareness, respect, and active citizenship.

4. Green Schools & Community Action Program
This program transforms schools into vibrant hubs for environmental stewardship. Using a hands-on, practical model, students lead projects in school gardening, reforestation, and community clean-ups, directly linking learning to sustainable development.

5. Youth Skills & Entrepreneurship Development
We bridge the gap between education and economic opportunity by providing youth and women with market-relevant skills training. Our curriculum encompasses technical and vocational skills, digital literacy, and essential soft skills to enhance employability and entrepreneurial success.

6. School Health & Well-being Advocacy
A healthy learner is a productive learner. We advocate for and educate on public health within schools and communities, promoting practices that ensure the physical and mental well-being necessary for effective learning and a high quality of life.

7. School Infrastructure & Learning Resources
We believe a conducive learning environment is fundamental.
